clue.text: Finishes with a Damien, Desmond or Douglas?

definitions.text: Finishes with a Damien, Desmond or Douglas?

parts.words: Finishes with a Damien, Desmond or Douglas?
parts.note: rhyming slang for degree classes: Damien Hirst is a first, Desmond Tutu a two-two, Douglas Hurd a third; people who finish university with one of these

explanation.surface: Someone finishing something alongside a man named Damien, Desmond or Douglas.
explanation.walkthrough: British student slang names degree classes after famous people whose surnames rhyme: a Damien (Hirst) is a first, a Desmond (Tutu) a 2:2, a Douglas (Hurd) a third.
explanation.definitionFit: Students who complete a degree course and receive a classified result have finished their studies and taken a degree.

clue.text: Going round club …

definitions.meaning: turning like a wheel, revolving about an axis
a ... Club, the international service organisation

explanation.surface: A golfer's club swinging round, leading into the next clues.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue into 3 and 4 Down: 2 and 3 together name a kind of aerial, so they also define 4.
explanation.definitionFit: Something turning on an axis moves round; the international service club for business people bears this name.

clue.text: … wrongly lied about 6 …

definitions.note: the ellipsis carries the definition over to 4 Down: with 2 Down this names a type of aerial

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the Teletubby's name
the letters of lied are put in the wrong order, rearranged

parts.note: 6 Down is TELETUBBY; Po is the smallest, red Teletubby

explanation.surface: Someone told a lie about a children's character, carrying on from the clue before.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue has no definition of its own: 'wrongly' rearranges LIED to DILE, which goes 'about' PO. The ellipses chain 2, 3 and 4 Down, where 2 and 3 together name a type of 4.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of aerial is a simple antenna made of two rods, so the linked aerial clue defines it.

clue.text: … sporting a real one (one of those looped round the middle)

definitions.note: plural: the antennas, whose name is spelt by the four three-letter entries circling the grid's centre; the answer is one of them

indicators.note: sporting suggests playing about or frolicking, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a genuine one, with a parenthetical aside about loops.
explanation.walkthrough: The ANT, ASA, TEN and ANN entries round the centre spell ANTENNAS, the things 'looped round the middle'. The 2 and 3 Down answers together also name a type of aerial.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is another word for a radio or television aerial, so this is one of the antennas.

clue.text: Letter the writer left in printer?

indicators.note: the writer and left are placed inside the printer brand

parts.note: Epson is a well-known printer manufacturer
the writer means the setter, I

explanation.surface: A letter that the author left inside the printer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like correspondence in the printer, but it is a character of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Model fashion magazine left out — fat character recently back on TV

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car

indicators.note: the left abbreviation is taken out of the magazine's name

parts.note: Elle is a fashion magazine
tubby means plump or fat

explanation.surface: A model quits a fashion magazine, while a fat TV character returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes one L from ELLE, leaving ELE. The BBC children's show returned in a new version in 2015.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po are the four creatures of the children's programme, revived on British television in 2015.

clue.text: Currents flowing round sides and top of electric fences

indicators.note: the river word goes around the letters from electric

parts.note: rivers are flowing currents of water

indicators.note: the sides of electric are its first and last letters
in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Electric currents running round the edges and top of an electric fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides and top of electric' gives E and C (its outer letters) then E (its top letter again), making ECE; 'round' puts RIVERS around it. Fences in the criminal sense handle stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is slang for a person who buys and sells stolen goods, which the law calls a handler or receiver.

clue.text: Explosive speech in The Mitre?

parts.note: HE stands for high explosive
an address is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A furious outburst in a pub called The Mitre.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mitre is a common British pub name, so the surface pictures a rant in a pub; the question mark marks a mitre as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is the tall pointed hat worn by a bishop, an example of ceremonial headgear.

clue.text: Default version of green energy

indicators.note: a version of the letters is a reworking of them, so they are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A standard setting for an eco-friendly power tariff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Default' reads as a noun, a standard setting, but is the verb meaning to fail to keep a promise.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back on an agreement or fail to honour a debt is to default on it.

clue.text: Good person to cruelly put down late offering from 30?

parts.note: ST, saint, a good person
to oppress is to keep down harshly

explanation.surface: A tyrant's plan to crush a good person, plus a late news item.
explanation.walkthrough: 30 Across is THE SUN, a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop-press item is late news inserted into a paper after printing began, something a newspaper like that offers.

clue.text: Satellite dish rented out, without Sky having the deal, initially

indicators.note: out signals the letters of dish rented are rearranged
without says some letters of that pool are left out of the result
initially takes the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A satellite dish rented, without the Sky TV package deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle DISHRENTED, then remove S, H, T and D, the initials of 'Sky having the deal', leaving the letters of the answer. Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Nereid is one of the moons of the planet Neptune, a natural satellite.

clue.text: Like our canines, can get bored?

definitions.text: Like our canines, can get bored?

parts.words: Like our canines, can get bored?
parts.note: canines are teeth, which a dentist may bore holes in; the surface suggests pet dogs becoming bored

explanation.surface: Our pet dogs can get bored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canines' pretends to be dogs; they are teeth, and 'bored' means having holes drilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth are able to be bored through by a dentist, so they are capable of being drilled.

clue.text: Slight oscillation of 4 in Queens

indicators.note: the number goes inside the two queens

parts.note: two queens: QU and ER are both abbreviations for queen
four is IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A small oscillation of an aerial in the New York borough of Queens.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' tempts as a reference to 4 Down; here it is the plain number four.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiver is a slight trembling movement, a small oscillation.

clue.text: Sip alcoholic drinks, some of Andy Murray's favourites

parts.note: a drop is a small sip of drink
shots are small measures of spirits

explanation.surface: A tennis player sipping drinks between his favourite strokes.
explanation.walkthrough: Andy Murray is a British tennis champion.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop shot is a softly played tennis stroke landing just over the net, a tactic Murray uses often.

clue.text: Quit a group supported by One Direction, originally

indicators.note: in a down clue, the earlier part sits on top of the later one, which supports it

parts.note: a band is a musical group

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone left a band backed by the boy band One Direction.
explanation.walkthrough: One Direction was a British boy band; 'One' is just the word itself here.
explanation.definitionFit: A place that has been quit has been left or deserted.

clue.text: I'd turned up to see dessert served up and shared out

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters of I'd are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the letters I and D
vide is Latin for see, used in references

indicators.note: in a down clue the pudding word is written upwards

parts.note: pud is short for pudding, dessert

explanation.surface: I arrived to watch a pudding being served and shared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' gives DI and 'served up' gives DUP, both readings upward in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something split into portions and handed round has been shared out among people.

clue.text: Intake of Peruvian tamanduas?

indicators.note: the letters are taken in by the two words, spanning their join

explanation.surface: What South American anteaters eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Tamanduas are anteaters of South America, so the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamanduas feed on insects such as termites and this small insect, their food.

clue.text: Leica stated old film rating

indicators.note: stated means spoken, so the camera name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Leica, the camera maker, is said the same as 'like a', whose synonym is 'as a'

explanation.surface: A camera maker announced an old rating for photographic film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stated' works on Leica's sound, 'like a', which is then swapped for its synonym AS A.
explanation.definitionFit: The American Standards Association number was the old rating for film speed, sensitivity to light.

clue.text: Number of lions eaten by 19, contrarily

indicators.note: contrarily means the letters are read the other way
the number is held by the written word, a run inside it

parts.note: 19 written as a word

explanation.surface: Rabbits eating lions, against the natural order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' finds NET held in NINETEEN; 'contrarily' turns it round. '19' looks like a reference to 19 Across; it is the number written in words. The Chinese tongue-twister 'Lion-Eating Poet in the Stone Den' gives the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Chinese tongue-twister the poet Shi devours this many lions, so it is the count he eats.

clue.text: Parts after Scotsman does, perhaps

indicators.note: the parts come after the Scotsman

parts.note: Rab is a Scottish man's name
bits are parts

explanation.surface: Pieces following what a Scotsman does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' reads as a verb but is the plural of doe, a female rabbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A doe is a female rabbit, so does are examples of these animals.

clue.text: Goes off trade bans by state boards

indicators.note: off says the word goes is removed

parts.note: embargoes are bans on trade
KS is the abbreviation for Kansas, a US state

explanation.surface: A US state imposes trade bans that a corporate board walks away from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes' looks like the definition 'leaves', but it is the letters removed from EMBARGOES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who boards a ship or plane gets on it, setting off on a journey.

clue.text: Girl with a heartless sister

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister

explanation.surface: A girl with a cold, unfeeling sister.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, such as a girl might have.

clue.text: Timeless "toy" that's blue, like 26

indicators.note: time is abbreviated T, so timeless removes a T

parts.note: the quoted word toy spelt T, O, Y with the O read as naught, zero, giving T-NAUGHT-Y

explanation.surface: A toy that never ages being rude, like the vacuum cleaner in 26.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks ask for 'toy' as written: its O, a zero, becomes NAUGHT. Noo-Noo, 26 Down, is the Teletubbies' vacuum cleaner, often in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means risqué or rude, and the Teletubbies call Noo-Noo badly behaved, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Either half of 6's rhyme, providing colour that is part of a hand

parts.note: pink is a colour
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A rhyme about a children's character, giving a colour to a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Either half of 6's rhyme' is a further hint: Tinky Winky, a Teletubby, has two halves that both rhyme with the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The little finger is called this in Scotland and North America, so it is part of a hand.

clue.text: Drunkards after almost 6 rounds?

indicators.note: almost drops the final letter of the name

parts.note: 6 Down is TELETUBBY; Dipsy is the green Teletubby
O is round in shape, so rounds are Os

explanation.surface: Drunks after nearly six rounds of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: '6 rounds' tempts as six drinks; 6 refers to 6 Down, a Teletubby.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipso is informal shortening of dipsomaniac, someone addicted to drink.

clue.text: City in the style of a 6

definitions.note: 6 Down is TELETUBBY; the definition names one of them

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a la, from French, means in the manner of

explanation.surface: A city built like one of the children's characters.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow Teletubby is named Laa-Laa, one of the four characters of the show.

clue.text: 12 holes for the 6s' 28

definitions.note: 28 Across is HOOVER: the vacuum cleaner of the Teletubbies

parts.note: 12 o'clock midday is noon
O looks like a hole, so holes are Os

explanation.surface: Twelve holes made for a vacuum cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' looks like a reference to 12 Across; it is the hour, midday.
explanation.definitionFit: In the show, the Teletubbies' blue vacuum cleaner robot is named Noo-Noo.

clue.text: One to kill 17 acrosses around 4am? Tiger, with no hesitation

indicators.note: around signals the letters are moved about, rearranged
with no says the hesitation letters are absent from the result

parts.note: 4am written out as four am
er is a hesitation sound

explanation.surface: A tiger acting decisively around 4am to kill ants.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell 4am as FOURAM, add TIGER, rearrange, and leave out ER. 17 Across is ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something that uses fumes or gas to kill pests such as ant colonies.

clue.text: It's mad, backing this president!

parts.note: mad reversed is dam: the famous dam in Nevada named after a US president, Herbert

explanation.surface: Someone calling it crazy to support this president.
explanation.walkthrough: The dam on the Colorado River is named after the 31st US president; 'mad' read backwards gives dam.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert of that surname was the 31st president of the United States, giving his name to the dam.

clue.text: Like the ref, Heather closely follows game

indicators.note: the heather word comes directly after the game

parts.note: whist is a card game
ling is a heather

explanation.surface: A girl named Heather tags closely behind a game, like a referee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a girl's name but is the plant, ling.
explanation.definitionFit: A football referee uses a whistle, so is often doing this, blowing it.

clue.text: Enthusiastic? Missing second half, lost rag

indicators.note: lost suggests letters gone astray, so they are rearranged
the second half of the word is dropped, leaving its first six letters

explanation.surface: Someone loses enthusiasm halfway and loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing second half' keeps ENTHUS from Enthusiastic; 'lost' rearranges it. A rag is slang for a poor newspaper; The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag is a slang term for a low-quality newspaper, as the British tabloid is often called.

clue.text: Look at dog's make-up

parts.note: to eye is to look at
to dog someone is to follow, shadow them

explanation.surface: Someone told to look at a dog's physical constitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' reads as a noun but is the verb, to follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic powder applied to the eyelids, one kind of cosmetic.
